transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Out on the trails and even back in town, I keep hearing and sensing things from the landscape telling me what to do with my work, and it’s starting to scare me. I just don't know what to make of it anymore.
Can you describe a specific instance where you heard or sensed something from the landscape that told you what to do, and how you felt about it at the time?

I was out on the trails when I heard this low, clear voice coming from the ridgeline telling me exactly which dancers to fire and what colors to paint my studio. At the time, during this really high, intense period, I felt completely convinced that the mountains had chosen me for some grand artistic mission and that it was all real. Now, though, it just terrifies me, and I've started avoiding those trails altogether because I'm scared of what I'll hear next.

During those times when you felt completely convinced by the voices, did you ever question whether the messages were actually coming from the mountains or if they might be your own thoughts, and how did that affect your behavior?

I didn't question them at all at the time because the voices felt absolutely true, and I was completely convinced I couldn't be wrong. Because they felt so incredibly real, I actually started avoiding certain trails and areas in town out of fear of what they would tell me next.

During the times when you were completely convinced by the voices, did you believe that others could also hear or sense these messages from the landscape, or did you think it was something only you could experience?

I'm not really sure, and I guess I hadn't even thought about whether other people could hear them at the time. I just felt like the messages were meant specifically for me because I was the one chosen for this special artistic mission.

Did you ever feel like the voices or messages from the landscape were controlling your actions or thoughts, making you do things you wouldn't normally do, or did you feel like you were still in control of your decisions?

I didn't feel like a physical puppet being controlled, but the voices felt so authoritative and urgent that I felt absolutely compelled to follow them. They gave me very specific instructions—like which dancers to fire or which festivals to skip—and because I truly believed I was chosen for this special mission, I felt I had to obey.
Have you ever had any periods where you didn't hear these voices or receive these messages from the landscape, and if so, how long did those periods last?

Yes, those voices and messages only happened during that first couple of months when I was feeling so high and revved-up. Once I crashed into this heavy, depressed phase—which has lasted for about nine months now—the voices completely stopped, even though the depression is still going on.

During the times when you were hearing the voices and feeling the messages from the landscape, did you also experience any extreme mood swings, such as feeling very high or very low, that seemed to be closely related to the voices and messages?

Yes, those voices and the feeling of having a special mission only happened during that extremely high, wired period when I felt unstoppable and barely slept. Once I crashed into this heavy, low depression, the voices stopped completely, even though this gray mood has dragged on for months now.

When you were experiencing those high, intense periods with the voices, did you also have other symptoms like excessive spending, reckless behavior, or increased sexual activity that went along with your elevated mood?

I didn't really experience things like reckless spending, hypersexuality, or dangerous behavior during those high periods. The only things close to that were taking on the initial business loans to open the studio and going on those late-night drives to trailheads to get choreography inspiration.

Did you experience any periods of significant depression or low mood before the high, intense period when you started hearing voices and feeling the special mission, or did the depression only start after the voices stopped?

No, the depression only started after the high period ended and the voices stopped. During that high phase, I felt completely unstoppable and wasn't depressed at all, but once I crashed into this heavy, gray phase, the voices went away while this awful depression took over.

Can you clarify if you have had any other episodes of abnormally elevated or irritable mood, aside from the initial couple of months when you heard the voices, and if so, how they compare to the duration and severity of your current depressive phase?

No, I've never experienced an intense, elevated phase like that before signing the lease and starting the studio earlier this year. That high period only lasted for about two months at the very start, whereas this heavy, gray depression has dragged on for about nine months now and feels so much more exhausting and harder to escape.

Have you experienced any other types of unusual perceptions, such as seeing things that aren't there or smelling odors that no one else can smell, in addition to hearing the voices from the landscape?

No, I haven't seen anything that wasn't there or smelled any strange odors. My experiences have been completely limited to hearing those low, clear voices from the ridgelines and buildings, and sensing those messages from the landscape.
Do you think the voices and messages from the landscape were a direct result of your high, intense mood, or do you believe they were separate experiences that happened to occur at the same time?

I think they were definitely connected to that high, intense mood, because they only ever happened when I was buzzing with energy and barely sleeping. Once I crashed into this heavy, gray phase, those voices and messages stopped completely, even though the depression is still going on. It really feels like they were just a part of that revved-up period.
Can you estimate how long the high, intense period with the voices lasted in total, and how that compares to the duration of your current depressive episode?

That high, intense period where I heard the voices lasted for about two months right after I launched the studio. But once I crashed, this heavy, gray depression settled in and has been dragging on for about nine months now. It feels like this low phase is lasting forever compared to how short that high period was, and I'm just so exhausted.

When you were experiencing the voices and feeling the special mission, did you ever have any moments where you doubted your own identity or felt like you were someone else, or were the voices and messages always about guiding your actions and decisions as the person you knew yourself to be?

No, I never doubted my identity or felt like I was someone else; the voices were always directed at me as myself. They focused entirely on guiding my choreography and studio decisions, making me feel like I had been specifically chosen and groomed for this grander artistic mission.
Did the voices and messages from the landscape ever tell you to do things that were harmful to yourself or others, or were they always focused on your artistic mission and decisions?

No, they never told me to harm myself or anyone else. They were always entirely focused on my artistic mission and studio decisions, like telling me which dancers to fire, which festivals to skip, or what colors to paint the walls. Even though they weren't violent, it was still incredibly scary and overwhelming to experience.

Looking back, do you think the voices and messages from the landscape were a primary experience that drove your feelings of being on a special mission, or were they more a reflection of your extremely high and intense mood at the time?

Looking back, I think they were definitely a reflection of that extremely high, intense mood. The voices and the feeling of being on a special mission only happened during that highly revved-up, sleepless period. Once my mood crashed into this low, heavy phase, those experiences stopped completely, which makes me realize they were closely tied to that intense state.
Did you experience any other episodes of psychotic symptoms, such as hearing voices, outside of the initial two-month period when you were feeling highly elevated and revved-up?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like that outside of that initial two-month high period. Once I crashed into this low, gray phase, the voices and the feeling of being chosen stopped completely. Even though this heavy depression has dragged on for months, those experiences haven't come back at all.
Do you think the voices and messages from the landscape would return if you were to experience another period of high, intense mood similar to what you had at the beginning of this year?

Yes, I definitely believe they are directly linked, since those voices and messages only ever happened when I was highly revved-up and sleepless, and then completely stopped once I crashed. It really terrifies me to think about, but I'm scared that if I ever get that wound up again, those unsettling experiences will come right back.

Do you think it's possible that your high, intense periods and the subsequent low, depressive phases could be part of a recurring pattern, such as bipolar disorder, or do you believe these episodes are isolated and unrelated to each other?

I definitely think they are connected as one wild swing, because this heavy, gray depression felt like the inevitable crash after being so unstoppable and wired. I hadn't really thought of the label "bipolar disorder" myself, but it makes complete sense that they are related since the low phase immediately followed that intense high. It really feels like a massive comedown from launching the studio.
Can you describe any significant changes in your energy levels, sleep patterns, or daily activities during the high, intense period, and how they contrast with your current depressive episode?

During the high period, I barely slept and stayed up until dawn, constantly pacing, choreographing, and even driving to trailheads at midnight because I couldn't sit still. Now, I feel completely exhausted, like my muscles are made of sandbags, and moving at all feels like dragging my body through wet cement. I either lie awake all night replaying my mistakes or sleep until the afternoon and still wake up feeling totally unrefreshed.

When you were experiencing the voices and feeling the special mission, did the content of the voices and messages seem to be directly related to your mood at the time, such as feeling grandiose or specially chosen, or were they more bizarre and unrelated to your mood or surroundings?

Yes, they were directly tied to how incredibly high and confident I felt at the time. Because I was convinced I was this absolute genius destined to change the dance world, the voices telling me which dancers to fire or which festivals were "beneath my purpose" felt completely aligned with that feeling of being specially chosen.
During the high, intense periods, did you ever feel invincible or have an exaggerated sense of your own importance or abilities that went beyond just being 'specially chosen' for an artistic mission?

Yes, I definitely did—I got completely convinced of my own brilliance. I even told my business partner that we didn't need a real business plan because my genius alone would attract investors and sell out our shows. I honestly believed I was on the verge of becoming this internationally famous choreographer who would put Bozeman on the global dance map.

During the high, intense periods, did you ever have thoughts or beliefs that were clearly unrealistic or detached from reality, such as believing you had supernatural powers or were a famous person, or were your thoughts and beliefs, although grandiose, still grounded in a possible reality?

Looking back, my beliefs were definitely detached from reality, even though they felt completely real to me at the time. I was convinced the mountains had chosen me for a special artistic mission to "wake people up" as a visionary choreographer, and that my sheer "genius" meant we didn't even need a business plan to become internationally famous. I truly believed we would attract massive investors and sell out shows on my talent alone.

During those times when you felt incredibly high and confident, did you ever question whether your beliefs about being specially chosen or destined for greatness might be exaggerated or unrealistic, or did they always feel completely true and justified to you?

No, I never questioned it at the time; those beliefs felt absolutely, 100% true and justified. Even though we were missing bills and my partner was incredibly stressed, I didn't doubt my destiny for a second or think it was exaggerated. It just felt like my absolute reality, and I was completely convinced I was right.
Can you think of any other times in your life, outside of the initial high period, where you felt an exaggerated sense of your own importance or abilities that seemed unrealistic to others?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like that before this recent period. That feeling of extreme confidence and believing in my own "genius" only happened during that high phase after I signed the lease earlier this year. I've never had another time in my life where I felt that way about myself.

When you were experiencing the voices and feeling the special mission, did you ever have any moments where you thought the voices were a result of your own mind playing tricks on you, rather than an actual external force guiding you?

No, not at all. When it was happening, it felt absolutely true, like an actual external force speaking to me, and I couldn't even conceive of the idea that my mind was playing tricks on me. Even though it was scary, I was completely convinced it was real.

Do you think that if your mood were to improve and you were to feel highly elevated again, the voices and messages from the landscape would return in a way that is consistent with your elevated mood, or would they be more disorganized and unpredictable?

Yes, I definitely think they would return in a way that matches that elevated, 'visionary' state. Since they only ever happened when I felt so grand and focused on my studio's mission, they would probably come back telling me what to do with my choreography again rather than being completely random or disorganized.
During your high, intense periods, did you ever believe you had a special connection to a higher power, or that you were destined for greatness in a way that went beyond your artistic mission?

While the connection to the mountains felt incredibly powerful and almost spiritual, it was always tied directly to my choreography and my artistic work. I never believed I had a connection to a religious higher power or was destined for greatness outside of the dance world. For me, the destiny was entirely about becoming a famous, visionary choreographer.

Do you think the voices and messages from the landscape would be considered a primary symptom of your condition, or more of a secondary effect of your extremely high and intense mood during that time?

I think they were more of an effect of my mood, because the voices and that special mission only happened during that revved-up, sleepless period. Once I crashed into this low, heavy phase, those experiences stopped completely, even though the depression has continued. It feels like they were bound to that high energy and couldn't exist without it.

During the high, intense periods, did you ever believe you were capable of achieving things that would have a significant impact on the world beyond your artistic mission, such as solving major problems or having a profound influence on society?

No, my sense of impact was strictly tied to my choreography and dance work. While I truly believed I was a genius destined to become an internationally famous choreographer who would 'wake people up' and put Bozeman on the map, I never had beliefs about solving world problems or influencing society outside of my art.
